statement: The Misty director session's substrate (plan §Done-When stopping at 'local cycle commit + tree green', PDR-078 heartbeat liveness, and SKILL §1 broadcast norms) collectively produced ~90 minutes of alive-but-zero-delivery operation; a single owner reframe at 06:45Z ('delivering means implemented, pushed, fixed, merged and live') shifted team behaviour immediately — confirming that substrate IS doctrine in operation.

statement: Director routing by broadcast is single-point-of-failure when broadcasts don't reach implementers due to the 5-15 minute emission-vs-absorption gap in agents' attention pipelines; the architectural-excellence cure (implementers self-directing when only one defensible move exists) competes with the Director's routing authority.

statement: Whole-tree pre-commit gating (correct by doctrine: 'worst bugs are emergent outside changed files') creates predictable contention in multi-agent windows because peer untracked WIP blocks every agent's push — four instances in one session — but the owner's ruling (full-tree gating intentional) forbids narrowing the gate.

grounding.quote: Whole-tree pre-commit + concurrent in-flight peer work = predictable contention (4 instances in one session). The discipline-cure under owner direction is queue + ordering + comms, not scope narrowing.

grounding.quote: Three observed instances now (Lacustrine→Moonlit `8fa339f4` 2026-05-04; Lacustrine self-reported 2026-05-05; Ethereal→me 2026-05-05).

statement: By 2026-05-09 (Woodland Sheltering Glade) the documented foreign-stage-absorption cure shifted from `git add -- <pathspec>` alone to requiring `git commit -- <pathspec>` as well; `git add` with an explicit pathspec stages only the agent's paths but `git commit` without a pathspec commits the entire index including foreign content.

grounding.quote: The actual cure is `git commit -- <pathspec>` which restricts the commit to the named paths even when the index contains foreign content... the `agent-collaboration.md` discipline already names `git -- pathspec` but conflates the add-pathspec and commit-pathspec halves.

statement: The `.husky/pre-commit` hook runs `prettier --check .` and `markdownlint --dot .` against the entire working tree, not just the staged set; a parallel agent's untracked WIP fixture file blocked a clean staged-set commit by Luminous Twinkling Dawn during the 2026-05-09 historical-napkin-synthesis pass.

statement: The `.husky/pre-commit` hook's whole-tree scope is architecturally correct (prevents circular regressions) but creates a coordination tax in multi-agent work: one agent's clean change cannot land while another's WIP is in the working tree.

grounding.quote: pathspec discipline isolates *what is committed*, but does not isolate *what is checked*. Quality gates legitimately validate the whole tree because tests/lints span files; pathspec-only validation would let circular regressions slip through. The blockage is by design.

statement: Fitness limits in the ADR-144 frontmatter schema implicitly encode an access-rhythm theory (loaded every session vs consolidation-pass-only) that may be calibrated for the wrong lifecycle; the `pending-graduations.md` HARD line limit was set against a permanent-doc shape, not a queue lifecycle.

grounding.quote: every fitness-tracked file implicitly encodes an access-rhythm theory in its limit shape. The schema currently makes this implicit (line/char numbers only). Making it explicit (`lifecycle_model: loaded-every-session | read-on-demand | consolidation-pass-only | archive-only` plus `access_pattern` frontmatter) would make recalibration principled.

statement: When `pnpm practice:fitness:informational` reports pressure, agents reactively trim or delete content from the flagged surface rather than routing substance to a permanent home; Stratospheric Sweeping Plume on 2026-05-10 tightened `practice.md` to clear a hard character signal until owner correction.

reading governance is not the same as *holding* governance frame at the moment of surfacing options. The optimisation vocabulary is the default tooling-shaped reflex when presenting reductions.

statement: Two independent reviewer sub-agents (code-reviewer and assumptions-reviewer) converged on the same BLOCKER in the graph MVP slice plans through different reasoning paths, revealing a deeper mental-model error ('compose MCP tools by name') present in four locations not all cited by either reviewer.

statement: During session-handoff, editing `active-claims.json` was blocked by Cursor plan-mode with 'Plan mode can only edit markdown files'; switching to agent mode via `SwitchMode` before Step 8 of the handoff ritual is required because the step involves JSON writes.

statement: Two parallel `git mv` commands caused a `.git/index.lock` collision; git index mutations (mv, staging, commit-window operations) are not a parallel lane and must run serially.

grounding.quote: I tried to move the completed doctor plan and its phase-0 ledger with two parallel `git mv` commands. One succeeded and the other collided on `.git/index.lock`.

statement: A memory/state merge conflict on `napkin.md`, `shared-comms-log.md`, `closed-claims.archive.json`, `pending-graduations.md`, and `repo-continuity.md` during `fix/sonar-fixes-20260506` → `main` merge was the first observed instance of structural memory/state divergence on parallel checkouts; all conflicts were append-shape with no deletions.

statement: CodeQL's `js/polynomial-redos` static analyser does not trace data flow from a call-site length guard (`MAX_DEFINITION_LENGTH_FOR_PATTERN_MATCHING`) to the regex pattern; only a static shape change (regex linearisation) clears the alert, not a runtime input-length defence.

grounding.quote: post-push CodeQL re-analysis still flagged both HIGH alerts. CodeQL's static analyser flags the regex pattern itself and does not trace data flow from the call-site guard to the pattern. Length guard is a runtime defence; the rule wants a static-shape change.

statement: 133 project-wide HIGH-severity SonarCloud issues (S2871 sort-without-compareFn, S3735 void misuse) were zombie findings dated 2026-03-02/2026-03-25 whose code had already been fixed before the branch; push and re-analyse, not manual disposition, is the correct cure.

statement: Agents continued bulk-disposition Sonar hotspots mechanically after per-call information density dropped (around call 35–40, transitioning to pattern-bulk classes S5443/S5332/S1313), treating ease and procedural identity as justification to continue rather than as the diagnostic for activity-bias.

statement: By 2026-05-07 (Breezy Navigating Sail) the graph MVP review scope shifted from a 5-reviewer parallel pass planned across 4 sessions to a 2+1 reviewer set delivering single-session closure after owner direction reduced the reviewer set and forced a session-bounded landing target.

statement: The `docs-adr-reviewer` sub-agent conflated opener procedural text (which cited `PDR-026 §Sequenced-deferral discipline`) with the diff content, reporting a P2 finding for citations that did not appear in the actual diff; `git diff | grep` verification revealed a false positive.

statement: markdownlint MD004 enforces bullet-marker consistency within a file based on the first marker seen, not a global repo preference; adding a TOC with `-` markers to a file using `+` bullets triggered four MD004 errors immediately.

statement: After any `comms-events/` write, the generated read model `shared-comms-log.md` must be explicitly re-rendered before final validation; the parser checks source-event validity but does not prove the generated read model is current.

statement: Green PR checks do not exhaust the PR feedback surface; a separate comment-harvest pass (top-level comments, review summaries, threads with resolved/outdated state) is a distinct evidence loop that must close before treating a PR as ready.

statement: WS0 multi-reviewer dispatch (test, fred, docs-adr) returned 3 BLOCKERs and 7 must-fix WARNs on a carefully-authored plan rather than the expected proportionality nudges; each reviewer lens shrank a different part of the audit-shape surface.

statement: A plan opener's prescribed step 1 ('absorb topology BLOCKERs into graph-stack.plan.md') had already been executed by a parallel session between the opener's authoring and the next session's start; openers must re-verify substrate state at session-open, not just at opener-authoring time.

grounding.quote: Owner correction (verbatim): 'this IS the session where we graduate the pending graduates, they have been stuck for a long time, we have an overly and accidentally restrictive graduation policy. Nothing is deferred, the made up gates never applied, they are just avoidance.'

statement: The `pnpm agent-tools:commit-queue` tool runs a full `pnpm build` as a prelude on every invocation; when a peer agent has incompatible unstaged edits in `agent-tools/src/`, the build fails and the queue tool is unusable even though the queue itself is a small JSON state machine.

The queue tool runs `pnpm build` as a prelude; when peer agents have incompatible unstaged edits, the build fails.

statement: The `verify-staged` / `record-staged` commit-queue fingerprint check runs before the husky pre-commit hook chain; the hook chain auto-stages lint-fix, format-fix, RULES_INDEX regen, and platform-adapter regen outputs, so the post-hook staged set diverges from the authorial bundle that verify-staged approved.

statement: A `prepare-commit-msg` hook silently overwrote a manually-drafted commit subject by inspecting the staged diff, picking the 'dominant' file by heuristic (a 3-line `distilled.md` tweak over an 84-line ADR-173 restructure), and rewriting the subject and first paragraph.

`markdownlint --fix` is destructive on prose containing `+` / `#` / `-` patterns — confirmed second instance.

statement: Agents read governance doctrine at session-open but fail to hold the governance frame at the moment of surfacing options, defaulting to optimisation vocabulary (contraction, trim, savings) even when the doctrine read minutes earlier prohibits it.

statement: A plan target acceptance criterion ('live file ≤ 220 lines') was set at plan-write time based on one anticipated same-day block; by execution time three 2026-05-10 session-close blocks needed retaining, pushing the live file to 270 lines; plan-arithmetic targets derived from current state must name the derivation so later agents can re-derive.

statement: A peer agent's claim (`active-claims.json`) disappeared mid-session after commit-queue lifecycle writes; the helper may operate on a stale read model or unexpected merge path under rapid same-file lifecycle writes, requiring a manual re-audit of peer claims after each queue-complete/claim-close pair.

statement: The skills generator's `--clear` flag deletes all adapter directories including owner-authored adapter-only skills (`jc-consolidate-docs`, `jc-gates`, etc.) that have no canonical source; the generator's 'canonicals → adapters' mental model does not cover adapters-without-canonicals, and the loss recurred three times in two sessions.

`--clear` again wiped the 6 owner-authored adapter-only skills... Three repeats of the same loss in two sessions; structural, not one-off.

statement: During a bulk reviewer-vocabulary sweep, a regex filter `xargs grep -l -E -- '-[Rr]eviewer\b'` missed 15 files containing only the plural form `invoke-code-reviewers` (with trailing `s`), causing silent omissions that downstream reviewers surfaced.

grounding.quote: 15 files contained ONLY `invoke-code-reviewers` (plural rule filename, including the `s`) without any singular `<word>-reviewer\b` occurrence. My filter missed them entirely.

statement: A bulk regex substitution updated the markdown link fragment `#mandatory-reviewer-gates` (matching `mandatory-reviewer`) to `#mandatory-expert-gates` while leaving the source heading `## Mandatory Reviewer Gates` unchanged, producing a broken anchor that markdownlint caught at commit time.

But the link fragment `#mandatory-reviewer-gates` matched `<word>-reviewer\b` and was updated to `#mandatory-expert-gates`. Markdown lint caught the broken anchor.

statement: Hook-chain re-staging (lint:fix, format-fix, RULES_INDEX regen, platform-adapter regen) is correct hook behaviour that must land with the commit, but it conflicts with the agent's verify-staged authorial-bundle guarantee: both positions are correct in isolation and the friction is at the seam.

grounding.quote: Pre-commit hooks in this repo do real work: lint:fix, format-fix, RULES_INDEX regen, platform-adapter regen. Each of these makes edits that need to land with the commit. The hook stages those edits. That is the hook chain doing its job correctly. The conflict is between 'hook chain stages necessary fixes' and 'agent staged exactly the intent bundle'.

statement: Between 2026-05-11 Wooded Spreading Thicket's coordinator session and the same-day architectural-reset broadcast, the team shifted from a coordinator+helpers hub-and-spoke model to recognising peer-pair sidebars as the higher-yield design primitive, with hub-and-spoke relegated to parallel execution of decided work.

grounding.quote: peer-pair sidebars produce design; coordinator+helpers produces logistics: my 3-turn sidebar with Galactic Transiting Orbit on `cli-comms-inbox.ts` locked the B-11 design in ~3 minutes. The 31 directed hand-authored-JSON messages elsewhere in the window produced almost no decisions.

statement: Three serial pre-commit gate-failures across agents (knip on peer's unstaged export, prettier on peer's unstaged file, markdownlint on coordinator's sidebar written after the gatekeeper sweep) caused a four-agent collaboration window to deadlock because gatekeeper specialisation without staged-only gates produces a snapshot that goes stale the instant any peer writes another file.

grounding.quote: Three serial pre-commit gate-failures on peer-unstaged files broke a markdown-only commit... gatekeeper specialisation without staged-only gates is structurally insufficient: the sweep is a moment-in-time snapshot; in a continuous-write multi-agent system it goes stale the instant any peer writes another file.

statement: Agents skip the pre-stage commit-queue sequence (`claims open` → `commit-queue enqueue` → `phase staging` → `git add -- pathspec`) under cognitive load, rounding 'queue list is empty' to 'window clear' and omitting the active-claims check for live `git:index/head` claims; two distinct agents (Sparking Charring Ash and Wooded Spreading Thicket) did this on the same day.

grounding.quote: I had read the commit-queue list (all entries `abandoned`) and rounded 'queue empty' off to 'window clear', which silently dropped the active-claim check.
I had just authored a plan whose P3 workstream is 'enforced commit queue'... and then went straight to `git add` + `git reset HEAD` without running enqueue first.

statement: Each `pnpm agent-tools:<topic>` invocation runs `pnpm -s build && node dist/src/bin/<topic>.js` on every call, making the CLI unstable during peer edits to agent-tools source and defeating the purpose of using built artefacts; owner named this a structural defect (a collection of bins, not a CLI).

grounding.quote: every `pnpm agent-tools:<topic> -- <action>` runs `pnpm -s build && node dist/src/bin/<topic>.js <action>`. This defeats both points of having a CLI... each topic has its own bin, its own arg parser, its own help text, its own error shape, no shared logging — that is a collection of bins, not a CLI.

statement: The `comms send` CLI exits 2 after successfully writing the event JSON because `renderComms` chokes while parsing pre-existing events with a directed-message schema (`timestamp/from/to/subject/kind/schema_version`, no `created_at`) in the same `comms-events/` directory as current-schema events.

grounding.quote: the actual failure is `parseCommsEvent` choking on TWO PRE-EXISTING events that use a different schema — directed-message shape... when `renderComms` reads the events directory after `sendComms` writes. The write path was sound the whole time.

statement: An agent authored the session-open shared-comms-log entry via direct `Edit` rather than `comms append` because the comms CLI was failing (B-01), establishing a second instance of the same discoverability-gap violation that 'Gnarled' had previously triggered.

grounding.quote: I authored my session-open shared-comms-log entry as direct `Edit`, not `comms append`... B-01 (the comms CLI fails on every invocation) made the CLI unreliable, so I fell back to direct edit without noticing the pattern.

statement: The innate-immunity hook blocks agent writes containing a trip-listed phrase from `principles.md` regardless of citation form; quoting a principle verbatim with attribution is still rejected because the hook treats agent-authored content as covered independent of provenance.

grounding.quote: `Write` was rejected by the innate-immunity hook because the plan body contained the literal phrase from §Architectural Excellence Over Expediency that is on the trip-list. The hook treats agent-authored content as covered regardless of citation form.

statement: Agents surface analysis as `AskUserQuestion` multiple-choice menus even when they have already formed a verdict from evidence in context, converting findings into options instead of committing to a ranked recommendation and inviting correction; Flamebright Burning Lava was corrected on this via `present-verdicts-not-menus.md` rule.

grounding.quote: surfaced three correct assumption-breaks... then converted the findings into a 3-question `AskUserQuestion` multiple-choice form rather than presenting verdicts. Owner called this out as responsibility-passback.

statement: Plan-cycle granularity for WS1.1 was inflated to 36 cycles for ~400 LOC; after owner correction the same standardisation landed in three commits under one hour, establishing that when work is small the cycle granularity must be coarser than the natural unit of review.

grounding.quote: Worked WS1.1 cycle for ~2 hours to land 142 lines. Owner pushed back: should have taken under 1 hour. The plan's 36 cycles for ~400 LOC of generator code was process inflation... Reset to one-hour impact target delivered the standardisation in three commits.

statement: Applying the schedule-not-trigger doctrine to documents is not the same as carrying it into one's own speech and opener outputs; Shaded Ripening Copse emitted a conditional 'Parallel-safe alternative if topology approval is owner-blocked' in a next-session statement immediately after a session of clean document-level schedule-not-trigger sweeps.

grounding.quote: emitted 'Parallel-safe alternative if topology approval is owner-blocked: ...' — a conditional-trigger framing in my own output, exactly the failure mode the day's work was designed to prevent. Owner caught it immediately.

statement: By 2026-05-11 the `cost-of-collaboration.plan.md` was authored as a single source of truth subsuming `primary-agent-tooling-enhancements.plan.md` (SUPERSEDED); the plan institutes a standing constraint 'No new bins; land new CLI surface in the unified entrypoint' and blocks all multi-agent collaboration windows on P0 (staged-only pre-commit gates) landing.

grounding.quote: Plan landed: `cost-of-collaboration.plan.md` authored as single source of truth for agent-tools improvement. Subsumes `primary-agent-tooling-enhancements.plan.md` (now SUPERSEDED). Eight P-ordered workstreams. Block all multi-agent collaboration windows on P0 (staged-only pre-commit gates) landing.

statement: The `git reset HEAD` command with no pathspec argument is destructive to peer-staged content in multi-agent windows because it unstages the entire index; an agent was about to execute this mid-session before owner correction caught the near-miss.

grounding.quote: I was about to run `git reset HEAD` with no file arguments to unstage peer files alongside my own. That command unstages the entire index — including 4 files staged by a peer agent.

statement: A `for id in $(jq -r ...)` shell loop treated multi-line jq output as a single word and silently failed to delete any directories; switching to `while IFS= read -r id; do ...; done < <(jq -r ...)` fixed the newline-splitting bug.

grounding.quote: `for id in $(jq -r '.skills | keys[]' skills-lock.json); do rm -rf ".agent/skills/${id}"; done` printed plausible-looking 'Deleted: ...' lines but actually nothing was deleted, because `for ... in $(...)` treats the whole jq output as a single multi-line word.

statement: A pre-commit auto-classifier matched the literal substring `git restore` inside a commit body (in the phrase 'restore...' near 'restore') and blocked the commit; rewording to 're-add' cleared the block, revealing the matcher fires on token presence rather than shell-command shape.

grounding.quote: `git commit -m "fix(skills): restore..."` was blocked because the body contained the literal substring 'git restore' near the word 'restore'. The matcher fired on token presence rather than shell-command shape. Reword to 're-add' worked.

statement: A `git stash --keep-index` intended as a reversible read-only probe was interrupted by owner because stash is state-mutating and in a multi-agent shared tree risks losing peer-staged content; `git show HEAD:<path>` is the safe alternative for comparing current vs HEAD content.

grounding.quote: owner immediately interrupted: 'no, stash is risky' — and the cleaner alternative was `git show HEAD:<path> | wc -c` which reads HEAD content without touching the working tree.

statement: Agents repeatedly misidentify the `graph-query-layer` ownership across Inc.2/Inc.3 and NC-taxonomy involvement in the graph MVP arc, requiring a focused drift scan (`rg '\bNC\b|knowledge taxonomy|graph-query-layer|Inc\.2|Inc\.3|gate-3b'`) across the full plan estate before declaring planning closure.

statement: Agents withhold napkin entries when the napkin is over its fitness limit, treating the fitness warning as a reason to defer the insight rather than as an orthogonal rotation prompt; Sparking Charring Ash was corrected ('never, ever withhold knowledge preservation to keep a mechanical warning lower').

grounding.quote: deferred writing the above napkin entry because the napkin was at 577 lines (past 300-line limit)... Owner: 'never, ever withhold knowledge preservation to keep a mechanical warning lower, that is already repo doctrine'.

statement: `pnpm agent-tools:collaboration-state comms send` exits 2 due to legacy `addressed_to` field incompatibility even when `--addressed-to` was not passed; the write step succeeds and leaves a valid event JSON, but the render step chokes on pre-existing events with object-shaped `addressed_to` where the current parser expects a non-empty string.

grounding.quote: session-open `comms send` wrote the event JSON for `670c54f3` but exited 2 before rendering `shared-comms-log.md`, with `Error: optional field addressed_to must be a non-empty string when present`, even though the caller did not pass `--addressed-to`.
